items.statement: Git object identity requires object kind, hash algorithm, and full digest.
Commit, tree, and blob identities are distinct.
A revision role does not replace immutable commit identity.
Base and merge first parent may differ.
Parent ordering is semantically significant.
Parent multiplicity must not be silently discarded.
Mutable refs are observations, not immutable revisions.
Deleted refs do not invalidate former commit targets.
Ref observation time is distinct from Git commit time.
Stable repository identity differs from repository alias.
Exact repository path lexeme is case-sensitive.
Host filesystem normalization is not repository-path identity.
UTF-8 textual paths are a bounded subset of possible Git path bytes.
Revision-qualified paths require stable repository plus commit plus path.
Line spans and byte spans require different coordinate conventions.
Artifact byte offsets are zero-based and half-open.
Logical line spans are one-based and inclusive.
Diff hunks require separate old and new sides.
Added and deleted hunks require nullable side pairs.
Artifact line coordinates differ from artifact byte coordinates.
Locator coordinates do not encode review applicability.
Exact selected-byte digests are assurance evidence, not locator fields.
A locator does not prove path existence or repository membership.
A contract corpus can replay exact locator evidence offline.
Invalid vectors are necessary to protect no-coercion boundaries.
Explicit discriminators prevent first-match union collapse.
Corpus canonicalization is not production canonical serialization.
Source-only contract corpora can remain excluded from distributions.
A zero-count-anchor review concern can be resolved without expanding frozen nonempty-span semantics.
S1.P03 must compose provenance around existing identity, revision, and locator contracts rather than redefine them.

Base and merge first parent may differ.
Ordered parent topology preserves order.

Parent algorithms match the child.
Topology does not imply repository graph or reachability.
Ref namespace and name are explicit.
Ref observations are repository-qualified.
Ref observations are authority-qualified.
Ref observation time is strict UTC.
Observed-present requires a commit target.
Deleted refs may retain a former target.
Deletion does not invalidate immutable commit identity.
Unavailable, inaccessible, and unknown states do not fabricate targets.
Ref observations remain additive and immutable.
Symbolic refs and tag-object semantics remain unsupported.
Repository path is exact and repository-relative.
UTF-8 textual-subset limitation is explicit.
Path case and Unicode form are not normalized.
Stable repository identity is required.
Immutable commit identity is required.
Alias, ref, role, and topology are excluded from path identity.
Path existence and entry kind are not claimed.
Non-UTF-8 Git path bytes remain deferred.
Line spans are one-based inclusive.
Byte spans are zero-based half-open.
Line and byte coordinate types remain distinct.
Revision-line locator binds to a revision-qualified path.
Artifact-byte locator binds to exact parent digest and length.
Diff-hunk locator distinguishes old and new sides.
Added, deleted, and modified hunk shapes are supported.
Locator union preserves concrete type.
Columns are not fabricated.

Empty line spans remain unsupported.
Applicability, review, and causal semantics remain outside locators.
Revision-locator corpus v1 is published.
All 23 exports have contract coverage.
Valid vectors lock successful behavior.
Invalid vectors lock strict rejection.
Replay vectors reproduce exact retained evidence.
Evidence classifications remain distinct.
Corpus execution uses a safe explicit registry.
Corpus files and permissions are exact.
Corpus remains excluded from distributions.
